**Observations from test image:**
- Very close-up view of stem/pod tissue
- Prominent white/gray cottony fibrous growth (mycelium) covering the surface
- Numerous small black dots scattered throughout — likely developing sclerotia
- Tissue appears bleached/light gray underneath the fungal growth

**Reasoning:**
The dominant feature is the dense white cottony mycelial growth covering the tissue surface, which is the hallmark of White Mold (*Sclerotinia sclerotiorum*). The scattered black structures are consistent with sclerotia (survival structures). The White Mold reference images confirm this pattern — white cottony mycelium on stems/pods with associated darkening. Diaporthe would show pycnidia in more distinct linear rows, and Charcoal Rot would show charcoal-grey discoloration without this level of white mycelial growth.
